title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Picture 2's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($E000, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it for a picture number with bit 7 set, as show_picture_e000 $041C asks): the base frame at +$0063, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0021, channel 2's script at +$003D and channel 3's script at +$0053.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 6 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 1, frame 2 then 1, frame 2 then 25, frame 2 then 5, frame 2 then 5, frame 1 then 15. One pass takes 52 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 9 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 4 then 5, frame 4 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 4 then 3. One pass takes 15 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 7 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 3, frame 5 then 3, frame 6 then 9, frame 6 then 3, frame 5 then 2, frame 5 then 12, frame 5 then 9. One pass takes 41 steps.

Channel 3's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 5 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 15, frame 7 then 5, frame 7 then 25, frame 7 then 3, frame 7 then 9. One pass takes 57 steps.

Picture 2's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 47 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 2, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1 and 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 2 bitmap bytes in all, in column 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 2, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 2, 3, 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 3 bitmap bytes in all, in column 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 2, named by channel 1's entry 1, channel 2's entry 1 and channel 3's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 4 of picture 2, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 9 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 6 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 2, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 2, 5, 6 and 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 16 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 2, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 3 and 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 12 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 2, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 3's entries 2, 3, 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 2 bitmap bytes in all, in column 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

The last byte picture 2's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,016th byte from $E000: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. It is the same on every side that holds the picture, and nothing reads it.
